walkthroughs.body_html:
In Britain the Suffragettes from 1903 used militant protest — speeches, smashing windows, hunger strikes.

In 1918 women over 30 with property won the vote. In 1928 it became equal to men's at age 21.

From the 1950s African Americans challenged Jim Crow laws.

Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in 1955. The Montgomery Bus Boycott followed. Martin Luther King Jr led peaceful marches and gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963.

From 1948 South Africa's government enforced apartheid — separating people by race in housing, schools and voting.

Nelson Mandela led the African National Congress (ANC). He was jailed for 27 years and released in 1990. Apartheid ended officially in 1994.

mcqs.q: What did Brown v Board of Education decide in 1954?
options: Brown v Board of Education immediately desegregated all schools in America.
The Supreme Court ruled that 'separate but equal' schools were inherently unequal, overturning Plessy v Ferguson and beginning legal dismantling of school segregation.
Brown v Board ended slavery in the southern states.
Rosa Parks was the lawyer who argued Brown v Board.

mcqs.q: Was Rosa Parks's refusal to give up her bus seat a spontaneous act?
options: Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
Rosa Parks was just a tired seamstress who refused on impulse to give up her seat.
Rosa Parks was the lawyer who argued Brown v Board.
No — Parks was a trained NAACP activist; the boycott was organised by long-standing civil rights networks that turned her arrest into a planned campaign.

mcqs.q: How was the US civil rights movement achieved?
options: Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' speech ended segregation.
Rosa Parks was the lawyer who argued Brown v Board.
Through decades of mass organising — NAACP legal work, grassroots campaigns, sit-ins, freedom rides — alongside leaders like King and Malcolm X.
